paper_metadata.title: Microstructure Evolution and Strengthening Mechanism of AlCrFe2NiCuMox High Entropy Alloys

evidence.quote: The AlCrFe2NiCuMox multiphase high entropy alloys were designed, prepared and characterized.
AlCrFe2NiCuMo x (x = 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2 and 1.4) (simply referred to as Mo0.6, Mo0.8, Mo1.0, Mo1.2, Mo1.4) high entropy alloys were produced by arc melting.

There are three phases formed in Mo0.6 and Mo0.8 alloys, which are disordered body-centered cubic phase (BCC phase), ordered body-centered cubic phase (B2 phase) and disordered face-centered cubic phase (FCC phase).

it is the AlNi intermetallic compound phase, and the crystal structure is the B2 structure.
With the increase of Mo element, the fraction of B2 phase increases.

With the increase of Mo element, the intensity of the diffraction peaks of B2 phase becomes the strongest, which indicates that B2 phase is the dominant phase in Mo1.0 alloy.
In addition, there is one new σ phase formed in Mo1.0 alloy. ... The diffraction peaks of σ phase match well with FeMo phase which belongs to the space lattice group of P42/mmm (136).
With the further increase of Mo element, according to the intensity of diffraction peaks, the fraction of σ phase also further increases in Mo1.2 and Mo1.4 alloys.

The microstructure of Mo0.6 exhibits the typical dendritic structure, while the microstructure is very complex at high magnification.
